article.name: basemode

contact.note: No published contact email was found in the checked official README, SECURITY.md, or SUPPORT.md. Example configuration values were not treated as project contacts.

article.summary: A local Rust CLI and Claude Code hook integration that stores project, decision, note, rule, document, and code-structure knowledge in an RDF graph and injects selected context at relevant events. This source review is not a benchmark or runtime assessment.

sources.label: Graph storage, merged reads and writes
Notes: create, recall, update and remove
Stop hook and code map refresh

who_what.text: The official repository describes basemode as a single Rust binary that maps a workspace into a knowledge graph and integrates with Claude Code hooks. It is local CLI and hook software with an embedded dashboard and optional extensions, rather than a hosted memory service.

architecture.text: The README identifies Oxigraph as an embedded RDF store, SPARQL for queries and updates, and N-Quads files for persistence. Reads load global and nearest-workspace graph tiers into one in-memory store when present.

Notes and decisions are typed graph resources with text or name/rationale, status and timestamps, and optional links to domains, projects or entities. Markdown and code extraction add graph entities and relations with source-file metadata where available.

Claude Code hooks gather session-start signals, match prompt context, and add pre-tool or post-tool file context. Stop can refresh touched code maps asynchronously. Hook output is fitted to configured budgets.

behavior.text: Write: learn creates a note with note text, type, active status, creation time, and optional domain/project/entity links in the current workspace graph. Decision logging stores decision text and rationale, optionally linked to a domain.

Update and correction: note text can be replaced by slug. Supersession retains old and new records and writes replacement edges and a status label together; serving reads filter by the edge. This is not general temporal validity or claim verification.

Delete: note removal deletes its triples from the current workspace graph. Stale-note purge uses lastRead age; the guide documents preview by default and backup before applying. Cleanup of exports, backups, synced copies, or every entity type is unverified.

Retrieval: explicit recall searches note text or domain links. Hooks match graph context against prompts and touched paths, then fit context blocks to budgets; match logs record matches, served and cut items, scores, and withholding reasons. Recall quality was not measured.

Scope: merged reads include the global tier and nearest workspace tier. The reviewed code does not establish tenant authorization or cross-user isolation; the workspace scoping document is design context that also contains planned requirements.

metrics.evidence: Keyword/domain recall and prompt-context matching are source-visible; no adjudicated questions or abstention probes were run.
Supersession chains preserve explicit replacement history, but no correction-accuracy or stale-value measurement was performed.
Note deletion and usage-based purge paths exist; no post-delete probe was run and backup/export cleanup is unverified.
Reads combine the global tier with the current workspace tier. No tenant-authorization review or cross-scope probe was run.
Graph relations and source-file metadata provide some provenance; no claim-support adjudication or citation-coverage measurement was run.

metrics.domain: Latency, write-to-recall delay, tokens, cost, and storage
metrics.evidence: In-memory graph loads, output budgets, and match logging are visible; no runtime latency, token, cost, storage, or write-to-recall measurements were collected.

limits.text: This is a bounded read-only inspection of selected sources at the verified main head. The system was not executed; answer quality, abstention, deployed access controls, end-to-end deletion, sync reliability, and runtime efficiency remain unknown.
The curated Atlas entry is used only for ordinal, listed locator, and source attribution; Atlas descriptions, marks, prose, and layout are not assessment evidence.

benchmark.text: Benchmark status is not_run. Project metric definitions, fixture, and execution-status record describe the separate project protocol; they are not basemode measurements.
